content.user_title: Manage GitHub Issues with Structured Triage
content.value_statement: Open source maintainers need consistent issue validation before labels, comments, or closures. This skill provides structured GitHub workflows for triage, responses, planning, and pull request coordination.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes bug reports, feature requests, questions, and documentation issues.
Checks code, history, and related issues before recommending labels or closure.
Drafts maintainer responses with validation results, links, and next steps.
Provides GitHub CLI workflows for listing, labeling, commenting, closing, and reopening issues.
Plans feature and bug implementations with affected files, dependencies, effort, and pull request links.
Defines label taxonomy for type, priority, status, scope, and special issue labels.
limitations: It is tailored to the Logseq Template Graph project and its module structure.
GitHub operations require repository access, authentication, and user confirmation.
It cannot verify issues without current repository files, history, and issue data.
It provides workflow guidance, not a standalone automation service.

use_cases.title: Triage New Reports
use_cases.description: Review a new GitHub issue, check for duplicates, assign labels, and draft a clear maintainer response.

use_cases.title: Plan Accepted Work
use_cases.description: Turn a valid bug or feature request into implementation steps, dependencies, affected files, and pull request guidance.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Issue Lifecycle
use_cases.description: Link related issues, track blockers, update status comments, and close resolved or duplicate reports with evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Triage a New Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Review issue #[number]. Summarize the report, identify the issue type, suggest labels, and list what must be validated next.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Bug Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate issue #[number] as a bug report. Check current implementation, related issues, and git history. Draft a response with evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Feature Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze feature request #[number]. Confirm whether it already exists, find dependencies, estimate effort, and propose an implementation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Fix and PR
prompt_templates.prompt: For accepted issue #[number], plan branch creation, labels, progress comments, pull request text, test notes, and closing language.

output_examples.input: Review a duplicate feature request for a class that already exists.
output_examples.output: The response explains that the feature exists, cites the current file and version, links the original issue, and recommends closing as duplicate.

output_examples.input: Plan a valid bug fix for an incorrect property setting.
output_examples.output: The result confirms the bug, lists affected files, proposes tests, assigns labels, and outlines a pull request that closes the issue.

output_examples.input: Handle a feature request blocked by a larger module change.
output_examples.output: The response maps blockers, links related issues, recommends implementation order, and asks the maintainer to confirm the preferred scope.

best_practices: Verify issue claims with code, history, and related issues before labeling.
Use comments that cite evidence and explain why an issue is accepted, blocked, or closed.
Confirm before running GitHub actions that close issues, push branches, or create pull requests.
anti_patterns: Do not close issues solely because they look similar to another report.
Do not apply labels without checking the requested scope and current implementation.
Do not run mutating GitHub CLI commands without repository access and user approval.

faq.question: What project is this skill designed for?
faq.answer: It is designed for Logseq Template Graph, with workflows and examples based on that repository structure.

faq.question: Does it run GitHub commands automatically?
faq.answer: It provides GitHub CLI workflows and command examples. Actual command execution depends on the AI tool, permissions, and user confirmation.

faq.question: Can it close issues?
faq.answer: It can guide issue closure for duplicates, resolved reports, and invalid reports. Maintainers should confirm before any closure action.

faq.question: Can it help create pull requests?
faq.answer: It can plan branches, pull request text, labels, comments, and closing references for accepted issues.

faq.question: Is the GitHub CLI required?
faq.answer: The documented workflows assume the GitHub CLI for issue and pull request operations.

faq.question: Can it handle feature requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks existing implementation, related issues, dependencies, scope, affected files, and implementation effort.
